ai_patterns_removed: Krishna's instruction speech unwound: 'the celestial route, as the blessed go' kept but shortened to 'the celestial road — the way the blessed travel'; the doctrinal chain ('pairs of opposites... beyond the three paths, beyond the strands of nature') regraded into plain clauses a 9-12yo can follow (bear pleasure and pain alike, senses in hand) with the 'three paths / strands' promise intact once instead of twice
'He placed the Lord within his own heart' simplified to 'He carried Krishna in his heart' (Krishna kept plain per house voice)
two doctrinal tail echoes of 'beyond the three paths... everything that binds' collapsed into one so the close does not preach
child_friendly_changes: standalone open: the farewell teaching named as the Uddhava Gita and Uddhava identified as the friend Krishna trusted most, so a first reader knows who is leaving and why
Badari anchored as a hermitage in the far north on the river Alakananda with 'the sight of the river washes every stain away' kept
Uddhava's role kept and clarified (carried messages between Krishna and the Pandavas); Vidura glossed as the wise uncle of the Pandavas
risk: Krishna's parting instruction (BP 11.29.40-47) simplified in wording but every element kept: go to Badari, the celestial route, the Alakananda and its cleansing sight, the solitude made holy by Narayana and Nara, patient endurance, gentle conduct, controlled senses, and 'meditating on me, you will come to me beyond the three paths'. The three circumambulations, feet-on-head farewell, and the carrying of the sandals are unchanged.

ai_patterns_removed: Narada named and placed at the open (the wandering sage who roams from world to world) so the recitation has a speaker a first reader can picture before the name-roll begins
deeds catalogue broken out of run-on blocks into short clauses with two orienting beats: 'The list began on the earth and never ran out of names' and 'The other worlds had fared no better'
trailing theology compressed to a single closing image: union with Narayana, Soma and Surya kept as 'fire returns to fire', nothing else piled on
child_friendly_changes: Sandipani glossed as Krishna's own teacher, Yama as king of the dead, Varuna as lord of the waters; Shalwa glossed as making war from the flying city of Shoubha
'this city built by Vasudeva' rendered 'this city that Krishna had built' (Vasudeva here is the patronymic and would be confused with Krishna's father of the same name)
Rukmini's car 'blazed like the sun and rumbled like a cloud' kept; the dwarf-form line about Bali kept plain
risk: Every name of the Harivamsha (1.249) recitation kept in the file's order — Mura, Nisumva, Naraka, Pragyotish, Panchajanya, Rukmi, Rukmini, Jaruthi, Ahdriti, Kratha, Shishupala, Dantavakra, Shatadhanwa, Shalwa, Shoubha, Dyumutsena, Gopati, Talaketu, Ravana's followers, Hansa, Dimvaka, Varanasi, Maya, Indrasena's son, Varuna at Lohitakuta, Parijata, the five kings, Kaliya, Yama and Sandipani's son, Bali, Kamsa's courtiers Peetha/Paithika/Asitoma, the Daityas Jambha/Airavata/Virupa, then Arjuna/Drona/Bhishma/Karna/Suyodhana and Suveera's daughter for Vabhru. Prophecy kept item for item: ocean devours Bhogavati and Dwaraka; 'There is none among gods, demons or men... save the slayer of Madhu himself'; regulations among the Dasharhas; union with Narayana, Soma and Surya.

'the thing their joke had called into being' tightened; double 'so that nothing of the curse might remain' construction simplified
child_friendly_changes: Dwaraka named at the open and Samba identified as Krishna's son by his wife Jambavati (file left him unexplained beyond 'son of Jambavati')
the Yadu boys identified as young men of Krishna's own clan mocking holy men
grinding-to-powder, sea-scattering, fish-swallows-fragment, hunter's-arrow chain kept step for step; Ugrasena named as the Yadava king
risk: 'He gathered the Vrishnis to him' rephrased as 'He summoned the Vrishnis to him' so the muster matches the source event (Mbh 16.1: Krishna, informed, summoned the Vrishnis) rather than reading as an invented gathering; the sages having spoken 'knowing the mind of the Lord' (BP 3.3.23) is preserved.

ai_patterns_removed: single ~170-word closing block split into three paragraphs (the curse as pretext / the 'unbearable' word / Uddhava's memory) for breath
redundant door metaphor collapsed — 'Only Krishna heard the door opening' said once instead of twice with 'had known what stood behind it all along'
judging-asides trimmed; 'as people do' kept once where it earns its place

'eighteen akshauhinis' glossed inline as 'eighteen full armies of chariots, elephants, horsemen and foot' (BP 3.3.13: aṣṭādaśākṣauhiṇiko)
risk: Krishna's verdict kept near-verbatim — 'When they quarrel among themselves, eyes red with wine, there is no other way to destroy them... When I act, they will vanish of themselves.' The no-war/crack-from-within logic, the sages' curse as the pretext, and the festive ride out to Prabhasa are all preserved.

ai_patterns_removed: rites sentence unwound so the serpent kings, sacred rivers and Varuna read as a procession instead of one 70-word chain (no material dropped)
'dwelt in so long' cadence kept once; no new AI habits introduced

Daruka glossed as Krishna's charioteer; Vabhru as a young chief of the clan; the summons to Arjuna and the Kurus kept
Sesha glossed as the thousand-headed serpent on whose coils Vishnu rests; Arghya glossed as the guest's offering of honor; payasa glossed as sweet milk-rice
